BiblicalUsage: The end is the limit of a thing, and Nebuchadnezzar's tree grows until its height reaches to the end of the earth. Daniel tells the king the tree is him, and his dominion reaches to the end of the earth. Darius decrees that God is the living God whose kingdom will not be destroyed to the end, and the little horn's dominion is taken away at the end.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the end in Daniel is always God's end, not man's. The tree grows to the end of the earth and is cut down, and the kingdoms of men end where God's kingdom begins. I hold that every earthly power has an end written into it, and God's kingdom has none.
